## What this does

Pulls breakfast and lunch menus from the [MealViewer](https://www.mealviewer.com)
API for a given school and writes them to a single `.ics` calendar file you can
import into Google Calendar (or anything else that speaks iCalendar).

The default behavior is **"give me everything from today through whatever future
menus MealViewer has published."** No manual date ranges, no clicking through
school websites.

### Pipeline

```
MealViewer API  ──▶  tibble of menu items  ──▶  one event per (date, meal)  ──▶  fallsmead_menus.ics
```

After rendering, open Google Calendar in a browser → Settings → Import & Export →
upload `fallsmead_menus.ics` → pick the calendar you want it on.

## Setup

```{r}
#| label: setup

# Install (one-time):
# install.packages(c("tidyverse", "httr2", "lubridate", "cli"))

library(tidyverse)
library(httr2)
library(lubridate)
library(cli)
```

### Configuration

Change `SCHOOL_KEY` to point at a different school. Find your school's key by
visiting `mealviewer.com`, searching for the school, and copying the slug from
the URL (e.g. `https://schools.mealviewer.com/school/FallsmeadES` → `FallsmeadES`).

```{r}
#| label: config

SCHOOL_KEY  <- "FallsmeadES"
SCHOOL_NAME <- "Fallsmead ES"
BASE_URL    <- "https://api.mealviewer.com/api/v4/school"

# How far ahead to ask MealViewer for menus. The API silently returns whatever
# subset of this window it actually has data for, so being generous is free.
LOOKAHEAD_DAYS <- 60

# Where the calendar lands. Relative to the .qmd file when rendered, or to
# getwd() when run interactively chunk-by-chunk.
OUTPUT_ICS <- "fallsmead_menus.ics"
```

## Step 1 — Fetch from MealViewer

MealViewer's API takes a school key and a date range formatted `MM-DD-YYYY`.
We chunk requests into 30-day windows to be polite and to avoid any quiet
truncation on the server side.

```{r}
#| label: fetch-functions

fetch_menu_chunk <- function(school_key, start_date, end_date) {
  url <- str_glue(
    "{BASE_URL}/{school_key}/",
    "{format(start_date, '%m-%d-%Y')}/{format(end_date, '%m-%d-%Y')}/"
  )

  cli_alert_info("Fetching {format(start_date)} → {format(end_date)}")

  resp <- tryCatch(
    request(url) |>
      req_headers(
        "Accept"     = "application/json",
        "User-Agent" = "lunchline/0.1 (R; tidyverse)"
      ) |>
      req_retry(max_tries = 3, backoff = \(i) 2^i) |>
      req_perform(),
    error = function(e) {
      cli_alert_danger("Request failed: {e$message}")
      NULL
    }
  )

  if (is.null(resp) || resp_status(resp) != 200) return(NULL)
  resp_body_json(resp)
}
```

Parsing is verbose because MealViewer nests its data four levels deep
(`menuSchedules → menuBlocks → cafeteriaLineList → foodItemList`). We
flatten it into one row per food item.

```{r}
#| label: parse-functions

# Parse one date from MealViewer's `dateInformation` block.
# It exposes both `dateFull` ("2026-04-07T00:00:00") and `dateKey` (20260407).
# We try both because individual schools sometimes omit one or the other.
parse_menu_date <- function(date_info) {
  if (!is.null(date_info$dateFull) && nchar(date_info$dateFull) > 0) {
    d <- suppressWarnings(as_date(ymd_hms(date_info$dateFull)))
    if (!is.na(d)) return(d)
  }
  if (!is.null(date_info$dateKey)) {
    d <- suppressWarnings(ymd(as.character(date_info$dateKey)))
    if (!is.na(d)) return(d)
  }
  NA
}

parse_menu_response <- function(api_response) {
  if (is.null(api_response$menuSchedules) || length(api_response$menuSchedules) == 0) {
    return(tibble())
  }

  # walk the four-level nest with map_dfr at each layer
  api_response$menuSchedules |>
    map_dfr(function(schedule) {
      menu_date <- parse_menu_date(schedule$dateInformation)
      if (is.na(menu_date)) return(tibble())
      if (length(schedule$menuBlocks %||% list()) == 0) return(tibble())

      map_dfr(schedule$menuBlocks, function(block) {
        meal_type <- block$blockName
        lines <- block$cafeteriaLineList$data %||% list()

        map_dfr(lines, function(line) {
          items <- line$foodItemList$data %||% list()
          map_dfr(items, function(item) {
            tibble(
              date           = menu_date,
              meal_type      = meal_type,
              cafeteria_line = line$name %||% NA_character_,
              item_type      = item$item_Type %||% NA_character_,
              item_name      = item$item_Name %||% NA_character_
            )
          })
        })
      })
    })
}
```

The driver function: start at today, ask for `LOOKAHEAD_DAYS` worth of menus,
chunk the requests, stitch the results together.

```{r}
#| label: scrape-driver

scrape_menus <- function(school_key = SCHOOL_KEY,
                         start_date = today(),
                         lookahead_days = LOOKAHEAD_DAYS,
                         chunk_days = 30) {

  end_date <- start_date + days(lookahead_days)
  cli_h2("Scraping {school_key}: {start_date} → {end_date}")

  windows <- tibble(
    chunk_start = seq(start_date, end_date, by = chunk_days)
  ) |>
    mutate(chunk_end = pmin(chunk_start + days(chunk_days - 1), end_date))

  windows |>
    pmap(function(chunk_start, chunk_end) {
      Sys.sleep(0.5) # rate-limit politeness
      fetch_menu_chunk(school_key, chunk_start, chunk_end) |>
        parse_menu_response()
    }) |>
    bind_rows() |>
    distinct() |>
    arrange(date, meal_type, cafeteria_line)
}
```

Run it:

```{r}
#| label: do-scrape

menus <- scrape_menus()

cli_alert_success("Got {nrow(menus)} menu items across {n_distinct(menus$date)} days")
```

Quick sanity peek:

```{r}
#| label: peek
menus |>
  count(date, meal_type) |>
  arrange(date) |>
  head(10)
```

## Step 2 — Collapse into one event per (date, meal)

Each `(date, meal_type)` becomes a single all-day event. We bucket items into
entrees / vegetables / fruits / grains so the description reads cleanly.

Each interesting entree becomes its own event (`Lunch 1`, `Lunch 2`, etc.)
so the title never gets truncated and your calendar day view reads like a menu.

```{r}
#| label: shape-events

# These show up every single day — they're always available, so listing them
# as their own event adds noise. They still appear in the description.
BORING_ITEMS <- c(
  "Grab N Go Yogurt & Granola",
  "Blueberry Chex Cereal",
  "Honey O's Cereal",
  "Banana Bread",
  "Mini Pancakes",
  "Maryland Made Cinnamon Roll",
  "Beef Sausage & Cheese WG Mini Bagel",
  "Beef & Cheese Spicy Taco",
  "Mini Cinnamon Cream Cheese Bagel",
  "Vanilla Belgian Waffle",
  "Grilled Cheese Sandwich",
  "Craisins",
  "Apple Juice",
  "Orange Juice",
  "Yogurt",
  "Cheese Cubes"
)

# Build the shared sides description (same for all events on a given date+meal)
build_sides_desc <- function(v, f, g, all_entrees) {
  parts <- c()
  if (length(all_entrees) > 0) parts <- c(parts, "ALL OPTIONS", all_entrees, "")
  if (length(v) > 0) parts <- c(parts, "VEGETABLE", v, "")
  if (length(f) > 0) parts <- c(parts, "FRUIT", f, "")
  if (length(g) > 0) parts <- c(parts, "GRAINS", g, "")
  paste(parts, collapse = "\n")
}

events <- menus |>
  group_by(date, meal_type) |>
  summarize(
    all_entrees = list(unique(item_name[item_type == "Entree"])),
    vegetables  = list(unique(item_name[item_type == "Vegetable"])),
    fruits      = list(unique(item_name[item_type == "Fruit"])),
    grains      = list(unique(item_name[item_type == "Grain"])),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    # Filter to interesting entrees for the title events
    headline_entrees = map(all_entrees, \(e) setdiff(e, BORING_ITEMS)),
    # If everything was boring, keep the first one so we still get an event
    headline_entrees = map2(headline_entrees, all_entrees, \(h, a) {
      if (length(h) == 0) head(a, 1) else h
    })
  ) |>
  # Explode: one row per headline entree
  unnest(headline_entrees) |>
  group_by(date, meal_type) |>
  mutate(
    n_options = n(),
    option_num = row_number(),
    # If only one option, just "Lunch: Pizza". If multiple, "Lunch 1: Pizza"
    summary = if_else(
      n_options == 1,
      str_glue("{meal_type}: {headline_entrees}"),
      str_glue("{meal_type} {option_num}: {headline_entrees}")
    ),
    description = pmap_chr(
      list(all_entrees, vegetables, fruits, grains),
      build_sides_desc
    ),
    # UID: date-meal-N so each option has a unique stable ID
    uid_suffix = if_else(
      n_options == 1,
      tolower(meal_type),
      str_glue("{tolower(meal_type)}{option_num}")
    )
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(date, meal_type, summary, description, uid_suffix)

events |> select(date, meal_type, summary) |> print(n = 20)
```

## Step 3 — Write the `.ics` file

A few things that were worth getting right:

1. **Idempotent UIDs.** Each event's UID is `YYYYMMDD-meal@lunchline.local` —
   stable across runs. Google Calendar dedupes imported events by UID, so
   re-uploading the same `.ics` updates events in place rather than creating
   duplicates. (The previous version of this script used `Sys.time()` in UIDs,
   which produced fresh IDs every run and caused exactly that duplication.)
2. **RFC 5545 escaping.** Item names contain commas
   (`Chik'N Nuggets w/ Green Beans, Corn, and Dinner Roll`), which would break
   the .ics format if dropped in raw. We escape them per spec: `,` → `\,`,
   `;` → `\;`, `\` → `\\`, newlines → `\n`.
3. **No line folding on DESCRIPTION.** RFC 5545 says lines should be ≤75 bytes,
   but Google Calendar's import silently drops continuation lines in
   descriptions, truncating them at the first fold. Google's own exported .ics
   files violate this rule too, and every major calendar client handles long
   lines fine. We still fold SUMMARY (which is short and works correctly).

```{r}
#| label: ics-helpers

# RFC 5545 §3.3.11: escape \, ; , and newlines in TEXT values
escape_ics_text <- function(x) {
  x |>
    str_replace_all("\\\\", "\\\\\\\\") |>  # backslash first
    str_replace_all(";",  "\\\\;") |>
    str_replace_all(",",  "\\\\,") |>
    str_replace_all("\n", "\\\\n")
}

# RFC 5545 §3.1: lines must not exceed 75 octets. Long lines get folded by
# inserting CRLF + a single space. We try to break at the last space before the
# limit so the .ics stays human-readable; if there's no space in the first 75
# bytes we fall back to a hard break.
fold_ics_line <- function(line, width = 73) {
  if (nchar(line, type = "bytes") <= 75) return(line)

  segments <- character()
  remaining <- line
  first <- TRUE

  while (nchar(remaining, type = "bytes") > 75) {
    # Look for the last space within the first `width` chars to break cleanly
    candidate <- substr(remaining, 1, width)
    last_space <- max(c(0, gregexpr(" ", candidate, fixed = TRUE)[[1]]))
    break_at <- if (last_space > 1) last_space else width

    seg <- substr(remaining, 1, break_at)
    segments <- c(segments, if (first) seg else paste0(" ", seg))
    remaining <- substr(remaining, break_at + 1, nchar(remaining))
    first <- FALSE
  }
  segments <- c(segments, paste0(" ", remaining))
  paste(segments, collapse = "\r\n")
}

build_ics <- function(events_df, school_name = SCHOOL_NAME) {
  dtstamp <- format(Sys.time(), "%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ", tz = "UTC")

  event_blocks <- events_df |>
    mutate(
      date_str = format(date, "%Y%m%d"),
      dtend_str = format(date + days(1), "%Y%m%d"),  # all-day events are exclusive of end date
      uid = str_glue("{date_str}-{uid_suffix}@lunchline.local"),
      block = pmap_chr(
        list(date_str, dtend_str, uid, summary, description),
        function(d, dend, u, s, desc) {
          lines <- c(
            "BEGIN:VEVENT",
            str_glue("UID:{u}"),
            str_glue("DTSTAMP:{dtstamp}"),
            str_glue("DTSTART;VALUE=DATE:{d}"),
            str_glue("DTEND;VALUE=DATE:{dend}"),
            str_glue("SUMMARY:{escape_ics_text(s)}"),
            str_glue("DESCRIPTION:{escape_ics_text(desc)}"),
            "TRANSP:TRANSPARENT",
            "STATUS:CONFIRMED",
            "END:VEVENT"
          )
          paste(lines, collapse = "\r\n")
        }
      )
    ) |>
    pull(block)

  header <- c(
    "BEGIN:VCALENDAR",
    "VERSION:2.0",
    "PRODID:-//lunchline//School Menus//EN",
    "CALSCALE:GREGORIAN",
    "METHOD:PUBLISH",
    str_glue("X-WR-CALNAME:{escape_ics_text(school_name)} Menus"),
    "X-WR-TIMEZONE:America/New_York"
  )

  paste(c(header, event_blocks, "END:VCALENDAR"), collapse = "\r\n")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: write-ics
ics_text <- build_ics(events)
writeLines(ics_text, OUTPUT_ICS, sep = "")
cli_alert_success("Wrote {nrow(events)} events to {OUTPUT_ICS}")
```

## Uploading to Google Calendar

1. Open [Google Calendar](https://calendar.google.com) in a browser.
2. **Settings (gear icon) → Settings → Import & export**.
3. Under **Import**, click **Select file from your computer** and pick
   `fallsmead_menus.ics`.
4. Choose the destination calendar (a dedicated "School Menus" sub-calendar
   keeps things tidy and lets you mute or share it independently).
5. Click **Import**.

When new menus get published and you re-run this doc, repeat the upload —
Google Calendar matches on UID, so existing events update in place and only
genuinely new ones get added.
